stem: When teaching about posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) recognition, which systemic symptom aligns with standard presentation references?

options.text: Weight loss never occurs with PTLD
PTLD always causes rapid weight gain rather than loss
Weight change is unrelated to PTLD presentation

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD clinical presentation may include weight loss along with fever, night sweats, lymphadenopathy, and gastrointestinal symptoms.

rationale_incorrect.B: Weight loss is specifically listed among PTLD presentations.
rationale_incorrect.C: Weight loss rather than gain is among cited systemic presentations.
rationale_incorrect.D: Weight loss is a described PTLD symptom requiring clinical evaluation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → PTLD → 3. Clinical presentation → e.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 6 → PTLD → 3.e. (weight loss among clinical presentations); PDF p. 281 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Weight-loss presentation angle distinct from diarrhea/weight-loss application item (cctc-2139) and PTLD recognition combo (cctc-2136); anchor verified on Cupples p. 281.

stem: When reviewing posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) during evaluation teaching, which fever-related statement aligns with standard presentation references?

options.text: Fever may be part of PTLD clinical presentation
Fever indicates PTLD only when graft tenderness is absent
Fever excludes PTLD when lymphadenopathy is present

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD clinical presentation may include fever along with night sweats, lymphadenopathy, and mononucleosis-like symptoms.

rationale_incorrect.B: Fever is specifically listed among PTLD presentations.
rationale_incorrect.C: Fever may occur with varied PTLD presentations and requires broader clinical evaluation.
rationale_incorrect.D: Fever and lymphadenopathy may occur together as PTLD presentations.

stem: A heart transplant recipient reports fatigue, sore throat, and lymphadenopathy resembling infectious mononucleosis. Which PTLD presentation aligns with standard references?

options.text: Mononucleosis-like symptoms exclude PTLD from the differential
Only pediatric recipients may have mononucleosis-like PTLD symptoms

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD clinical presentation may include symptoms that resemble infectious mononucleosis, along with fever, lymphadenopathy, and other systemic findings.

rationale_incorrect.B: Mononucleosis-like symptoms are listed PTLD presentations rather than excluding it.
rationale_incorrect.C: Infectious mononucleosis-like symptoms are specifically described in PTLD presentation.
rationale_incorrect.D: Mononucleosis-like PTLD symptoms may occur in adult and pediatric transplant recipients.

stem: A coordinator is updating PTLD recognition teaching. Evaluate the following statements about clinical presentation:

elements.text: Fever may be part of PTLD presentation.
Weight loss may occur with PTLD.
PTLD always presents with obvious graft tenderness and high fever in every case.

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD may be asymptomatic, and fever and weight loss are cited presentations. Statement IV is false because presentation is variable and may be asymptomatic or systemic without isolated graft tenderness in every case.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also true—weight loss is among listed presentations.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement IV is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false because PTLD presentation is variable and may be asymptomatic.
